stories.text: As the owner, I want every seat started, seen, stopped and warned from Lys, so that herdr and Argus can be switched off.
As the owner, I want to set a seat's words, variables, countdowns and schedules in one place and see what was actually delivered, so that overnight work runs without a second system.
As an agent, I want to read and set my own variables with a revision, so that my focus survives a compaction and nobody overwrites it blind.
As an agent, I want a reminder to carry the goal's words and the time left, so that I can plan the hour.
As an operator, I want to attach to a seat's terminal from Lys when I need to look, so that I do not need a terminal workspace program to own the seats.
As an operator, I want a supervised seat to keep working when its terminal, runner or identity service exits, so that a viewing or service failure does not end its conversation.
As an operator, I want to upgrade Lys while an active seat streams and receives control replies, so that the same seat continues under one proven owner.
As an operator, I want stored ownership and uncertain work to recover without replay and every failure to be proved by a signal-driven test, so that recovery does not invent success.
As an operator, I want counted work per seat to stay flat at three times the real roster, so that supervision remains cheap as the team grows.
As an operator, I want a deliberate stop to win over handover and the screen to name current ownership and unknown authority, so that I can trust what Lys says is running.
